newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP Hawaiian unit loses US$50 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: BHP Hawaiian unit loses US$50 mln deal.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Wednesday its Hawaiian unit had lost a three year contract worth US$50 million to supply petroleum products to the South Pacific island of American Samoa.
"The (contract) renewal came up recently, we applied for renewal but were unsuccessful," a spokesman from BHP's petroleum division told Reuters.
"There is a provision for us to appeal the decision that has been made - the likelihood is we will probably appeal," he said. The contract, which commences in January 1998, was won by Mobil.

The petroleum storage facilities on the island, which have a capacity of 300,000 litres of product, are owned by the American Samoan government and supply the island with petrol, marine and aviation fuels.
BHP has been the operator of the facilities since 1983 and under the current contract since 1994.
